| AC7 — resize vs set device | ✅ (with caveat) | `resize 1280 900` → `✓ Resized to 1280×900`, `innerWidth/innerHeight` = 1280/900. issues.title: eval cannot read page-defined JS globals — it executes in Browser4's isolated world, not the page's main world

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 -s emu open --headless http://localhost:18080/assets/geolocation.html
./b4w.ps1 -s emu eval "typeof window.geolocationPromise"        # -> undefined
./b4w.ps1 -s emu cdp Runtime.evaluate --json '{"expression":"typeof window.geolocationPromise","returnByValue":true}'
# -> {"result":{"type":"string","value":"object"}}  (same page, same moment)
# Proof of world separation: inject a <script> that sets window.__mw + document.title; a second injected script reads window.__mw into a DOM attribute; eval sees the DOM but not the global.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: eval runs JavaScript in the page (help: 'Evaluate JavaScript expression on page or element'; SKILL.md: 'Execute JavaScript in the page'), so page-created globals are readable — the documented way to read window.geolocationPromise.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: eval lands in a separate JS world: window.geolocationPromise is undefined, an injected main-world script's window.__mw is undefined to eval while a second main-world script reads it fine (round-tripped via a DOM attribute), and typeof __pulsar_utils__ === 'function' inside eval. A user following the documented workflow concludes the page never defined the promise. No warning or documentation mentions this.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: Dual-world evaluation: the driver's evaluation path resolves to the Browser4 isolated world (the one the runtime __pulsar_utils__ is injected into) instead of the page's main world. Browser4WebDriver.evaluate()/ensurePulsarUtilsInjected() re-establish a cached isolated-world context id, and the eval tool resolves through that; the actual world selection lives in the upstream pulsar-browser dependency (IsolatedWorldManager / DualWorldScriptLoader). DOM access and standard browser APIs are shared/re-implemented per world, which is why everything except page-defined globals appears to work.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: browser4-core/browser4-browser/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/chrome/Browser4WebDriver.kt:evaluate (line 2465) / ensurePulsarUtilsInjected (line ~2508); eval tool branch browser4-agentic/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/agentic/tools/builtin/BrowserTabToolExecutor.kt (line 2254); CLI CommandDef 'eval' in cli/browser4-cli/src/commands.rs

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Make the eval tool evaluate in the page's main world by default (CDP Runtime.evaluate with no contextId / the main-frame default context), as Puppeteer/Playwright do; keep the isolated world for the internal runtime and any helper that needs it.
- If the isolated world is deliberate (anti-bot stealth), expose an explicit switch (e.g. --world main|isolated, default main) and document the limitation loudly in help eval and skills/browser4-cli/references/eval.md.
- Detect the failure mode: when the expression evaluates to undefined for a bare page-global reference, warn that the page's JS globals are not visible from eval and point at the cdp Runtime.evaluate escape hatch.
- Add an e2e scenario that navigates to a fixture defining window.<x> and asserts eval can read it (the gap is invisible to DOM-only tests).

issues.title: set geo emulation is invisible to the page: geolocation permission is never granted, so getCurrentPosition never settles

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 -s emu open --headless http://localhost:18080/assets/geolocation.html
./b4w.ps1 -s emu set geo --lat 48.8584 --lon 2.2945 --accuracy 10
./b4w.ps1 -s emu reload
# read window.geolocationPromise from the page's main world -> stays 'pending' forever
# Workaround that fixes it:
./b4w.ps1 -s emu cdp Browser.grantPermissions --json '{"permissions":["geolocation"],"origin":"http://localhost:18080"}'
./b4w.ps1 -s emu reload   # now resolves to {"latitude":48.8584,"longitude":2.2945}

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: After set geo --lat .. --lon .. --accuracy .., a reload of the fixture resolves window.geolocationPromise to the emulated coordinates (AC1).

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The promise never settles (checked 3 s after load, and again after reload). Chrome requires the geolocation permission to be granted for getCurrentPosition to return a position; Emulation.setGeolocationOverride alone is not sufficient. The fixture supplies no error callback, so a denied/prompt permission produces an eternally pending promise rather than an error. Neither help set nor SKILL.md mentions granting permission; repo-wide grep finds no Browser.grantPermissions call anywhere in the product.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The geo branch of the CLI's set command issues exactly one CDP call — Emulation.setGeolocationOverride {latitude, longitude, accuracy} — and nothing calls Browser.grantPermissions for the page origin. Chrome's geolocation API gates on the permission, so the override is never observable to page script.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/commands.rs:2352-2360 (CommandDef set, tool_params_fn, "geo" branch)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Issue Browser.grantPermissions {permissions:['geolocation'], origin:<current page origin>} as part of set geo (the origin is available from the session's current URL), or add an explicit --grant-permission flag documented in help set.
- Document the requirement in help set and skills/browser4-cli/SKILL.md (the set row currently has an empty 'Full reference' column).
- Consider clearing the permission on a documented reset path so emulation is reversible.
- Note for the fixture authors: a fixture promise without an error callback cannot distinguish 'denied' from 'still pending' — adding an error handler would make this failure self-evident.

issues.title: goto under set offline on reports success (exit 0, 'Page loaded.') for a network failure

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 -s emu set offline on
./b4w.ps1 -s emu goto http://localhost:18080/assets/mobile.html ; echo $?

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: AC2: the goto fails with a network error — non-zero exit and a message naming the failure (e.g. ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED).

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Exit code 0. Output: 'Navigated to chrome-error://chromewebdata/ (redirected from http://localhost:18080/assets/mobile.html)' followed by 'Page loaded. If results render asynchronously, wait for the result element ...'. No network-error text anywhere in the output; the only hint is the chrome-error:// URL embedded in the 'Navigated to' line (no 'Possible blocked/challenge page' warning either). Reproduced twice; full output captured to .test-sessions/20261013T0154334271610Z/offline_goto_full.txt.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: Chrome commits an error interstitial (chrome-error://chromewebdata/) for a failed navigation, so the backend navigate tool returns success; handle_goto maps only tool-level errors to CLI failures and never inspects the landed URL (or the offline emulation state) after navigation. The post-navigation 'Page loaded' hint is printed unconditionally on the success path.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:handle_goto (~line 2832) — post-navigation validation / message selection; the backend navigate handler may also need to surface the net error.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- After navigation, treat a final URL starting with chrome-error:// (or a document.URL of chrome-error) as a failure: return Err with the page's own error text (Chrome exposes it under #main-message) so the message names ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED / ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED etc.
- Suppress the 'Page loaded' hint when the landed document is an error page.
- When offline emulation is active (set offline on was the last emulation command for the tab), append the likely cause to the error, e.g. 'navigation failed while offline emulation is enabled (set offline off to restore)'.
- Add an e2e assertion that goto under offline returns a non-zero exit code.

issues.title: Device-metrics emulation is silently discarded by goto (but survives reload, go-back and raw Page.navigate)

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 -s emu set device --width 390 --height 844 --dpr 2 --mobile
./b4w.ps1 -s emu eval "window.innerWidth+'x'+window.innerHeight+' dpr '+window.devicePixelRatio"   # 390x844 dpr 2
./b4w.ps1 -s emu goto http://localhost:18080/assets/mobile.html
./b4w.ps1 -s emu eval "window.innerWidth+'x'+window.innerHeight+' dpr '+window.devicePixelRatio"   # 1920x1080 dpr 1
# control: reload, go-back and 'cdp Page.navigate' all PRESERVE 390x844 dpr 2

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Emulation applied by set device stays in effect until it is explicitly changed or the session closes (or, if navigation is meant to reset it, the CLI says so and warns when it drops an active emulation).

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: A cross-URL goto silently restores the native window metrics (1920x1080, dpr 1); no message, warning or exit-code change. The same override survives reload, go-back, snapshot, page-info and a raw cdp Page.navigate to a different URL — so it is the goto path, not navigation itself. media/geo/headers emulation all survive the same goto, making the behaviour inconsistent across modes.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The reset happens in the goto/navigate pipeline (CLI goto -> MCP navigate tool). It is not in this repository's Kotlin: the only setDeviceMetricsOverride call sites here are in Browser4WebDriver.screenshotFullPage (which temporarily resizes and restores), and grep finds no clearDeviceMetricsOverride/resetViewport in the REST or agentic layers. The likely location is the upstream pulsar-browser dependency's navigate/load pipeline normalizing the viewport to the window size. Needs backend-side confirmation (log around Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride / clearDeviceMetricsOverride during navigate).

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:handle_goto (~2832) for the CLI path; server side not in this repo — suspect PulsarWebDriver.navigate in the pulsar-browser dependency (see browser4-core/browser4-browser/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/chrome/Browser4WebDriver.kt for the subclassing pattern)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Stop clearing/re-setting device metrics during navigation, or re-apply the tab's active override after the new document commits.
- If a reset is intentional, warn on stderr when a goto drops an active device emulation ('device emulation cleared by navigation — re-run set device ...'), and document the persistence rules per mode in help set.
- Add e2e coverage: set device -> goto different URL -> assert innerWidth/devicePixelRatio survived (mirrors the AC5/AC6 checks).

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:

./b4w.ps1 -s emu eval "window.devicePixelRatio"      # 2
./b4w.ps1 -s emu resize 1280 900                     # ✓ Resized to 1280×900
./b4w.ps1 -s emu eval "window.devicePixelRatio"      # 1 (emulation gone)

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Either the resize preserves the emulated device scale factor, or the output states that the device emulation was cleared.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The viewport becomes 1280x900 as requested, but devicePixelRatio silently returns to 1. The success message '✓ Resized to 1280×900' implies nothing was lost.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: resize (browser window resize) replaces/clears the CDP device-metrics override; the command reports only the dimensions it set. Related to the goto reset (issue above) — both are paths where the viewport is re-derived from the window without re-applying the tab's emulation.

sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Keep the emulated deviceScaleFactor across resize when one is active, or explicitly clear-and-report.

sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The unknown-mode branch in the CLI emits a deliberately unusable CDP call ({method: "", params:{mode}} with the comment 'emit an unusable call so the CLI errors early'), so the failure surfaces from the backend CDP layer as a protocol-validation error instead of a CLI-side argument error. The mode list is known statically in the same function.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/commands.rs:2396-2399 (CommandDef set, tool_params_fn, `other =>` branch)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Validate the mode in the CLI before building the CDP payload and fail with: "Unknown set mode 'bogus'. Valid modes: geo, offline, headers, media, device (see `browser4-cli help set`)."
- Include a nearest-match suggestion for typos (e.g. 'geoo' -> 'geo').
- Also reject mode-specific options that do not belong to the given mode (e.g. --dpr with set geo) instead of silently ignoring them.

issues.title: set commands print a bare {} on success — no confirmation of what was applied

sections.label: Reproduction
Expected Behavior
sections.body: A short human-readable confirmation naming the mode and the applied values (like resize's '✓ Resized to 1280×900' or cookie-set's 'Cookie set: b4test'), so the user can tell which emulation is currently active.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Every set invocation prints exactly '{}' (the raw execute_cdp_command result). Nothing identifies the mode, the values, or the target tab/session — a user cannot tell a successful call from a no-op, and there is no read-back command to check the active emulation state.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The set CommandDef maps to the generic execute_cdp_command tool and prints its raw JSON envelope verbatim; the CDP method returns an empty object, so '{}' is the whole output. There is no CLI-side formatting layer for this command family.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/commands.rs:2326-2402 (CommandDef set) and the generic execute_cdp_command print path in cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Print a mode-specific confirmation from the CLI, e.g. '✓ Geolocation emulated: 48.8584, 2.2945 (±10 m)', '✓ Offline mode ON for session emu'.
- Suppress the raw envelope (keep it for --json).
- Consider a read-back command (e.g. `set status` / `emulation` ) that lists the active overrides for the current tab — today there is no way to query them.

sections.body: An error when required values are missing — the help itself says for --lat 'give --lat together with --lon', implying they belong together — or at minimum a warning plus documented defaults.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Both commands succeed silently. set geo pins the simulated position to Null Island (0,0); set device shrinks the viewport to 390x844 (dpr 1, mobile off). Neither help nor SKILL.md documents the 390/844 fallback for --width/--height (help only mentions dpr default 1).

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The tool_params_fn uses unwrap_or defaults: lat/lon/accuracy -> 0.0/0.0/1.0 (commands.rs 2353-2355) and width/height/dpr/mobile -> 390/844/1.0/false (commands.rs 2387-2390). No required-argument validation is performed for these option combinations.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/commands.rs:2352-2360 (geo) and 2386-2394 (device)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Treat --lat/--lon as required for set geo and --width/--height as required for set device; error with the exact missing flag.
- If defaults are kept deliberately, state them in help ("--width ... (default: 390)") and echo them in the success confirmation (see the confirmation issue above).

issues.title: set headers --json with invalid JSON silently clears all extra headers (exit 0)

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 -s emu set headers --json 'not-json-at-all' ; echo $?
# exit 0, prints {}
./b4w.ps1 -s emu goto http://localhost:18080/b4/network-fixture.html
./b4w.ps1 -s emu network requests --filter network-fixture   # no X-B4-* header present

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: A parse error naming the malformed JSON, with no change to the currently active header set.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Exit 0 and '{}'. The malformed payload is replaced by an empty object, which Network.setExtraHTTPHeaders applies as a full replacement — so the command both misreports success and destroys previously configured headers.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: serde_json::from_str(...).unwrap_or_else(|_| json!({})) swallows the parse error and substitutes an empty header map.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/commands.rs:2369-2373 (CommandDef set, tool_params_fn, "headers" branch)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Propagate the serde error (or emit a CLI-side error) instead of defaulting to {} — a destructive no-op is worse than a failure.
- Only send Network.setExtraHTTPHeaders when parsing succeeded; add a unit test for the malformed-JSON case (commands.rs already has set-related unit tests to extend).

issues.title: Emulation scope, persistence across navigation, and how to undo are undocumented

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 help set            # zero mentions of session/tab scope, persistence, navigation, clear/reset/undo
./b4w.ps1 help                # DevTools section lists 'set <mode> [state]' with a truncated summary
# SKILL.md has one row: 'set geo|offline|headers|media|device ... Emulate locations, networks, devices, and media features' with an empty Full reference column

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Documentation stating (a) whether emulation is per-tab/per-session, (b) what survives navigation, and (c) how to clear each mode.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: None of this exists. Measured behaviour that users must guess: media/geo/headers survive goto and reload; device metrics survive reload/go-back but are cleared by goto (and by resize); offline is undone by 'set offline off'; media can be reset with --color-scheme no-preference; geo and device have NO CLI undo path at all (only 'cdp Emulation.setGeolocationOverride --json {}' / 'cdp Emulation.clearDeviceMetricsOverride').

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The set command family was documented as a one-line summary plus option list; the persistence semantics implemented by the backend/CDP were never captured in help text, SKILL.md, or a references/ page.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/help.rs (set help text derives from the CommandDef) and skills/browser4-cli/SKILL.md (command-map row for set)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add an 'Emulation' notes block to help set: scope (current tab of the session), persistence per mode, and the exact undo for each mode.
- Add a short section to skills/browser4-cli/SKILL.md (and optionally references/emulation.md) with a persistence matrix: geo/media/headers survive navigation; device metrics are dropped by goto and resize; declare the intended behaviour once issue 4 is fixed.
- Provide symmetrical reset syntax (e.g. set geo --clear, set device --clear) so no mode requires the cdp escape hatch.

issues.title: --help --examples for set claims the backend may be down instead of 'no examples yet'

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 set --help --examples
# Output: "No examples available for 'set' — is the backend running?"  (exit 0)

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Either the examples advertised by `help set` ('Runnable examples: browser4-cli set --help --examples') are shown, or a plain 'No examples available for set'.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The message blames a possibly-stopped backend even though the backend was running (every other command in the same session worked), and the command exits 0. It also contradicts help set, which advertises runnable examples.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The examples lookup has no static list for set and falls back to a generic message that assumes backend-provided examples; the exit code is not propagated.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/help.rs (examples lookup / fallback message)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Ship a static example list for set (the set CommandDef's option set makes good examples trivial: 'set geo --lat 48.8584 --lon 2.2945', 'set offline on', 'set headers --json ...', 'set media --color-scheme dark', 'set device --width 390 --height 844 --dpr 2 --mobile').
- Drop the 'is the backend running?' hint for commands with no backend-provided examples.

issues.title: Top-level and DevTools help truncate the set summary to a dangling '`set …' — media and device modes are invisible

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 help
./b4w.ps1 help devtools

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The one-line summary names all five modes (or at least reads as a complete sentence).

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Both listings end with: 'Emulate browser capabilities via Chrome DevTools Protocol: `set geo`, `set offline`, `set headers`, `set …' — the ellipsis lands mid-item inside an unclosed backtick, hiding 'set media' and 'set device' from the primary discovery surface.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The description string is truncated at a fixed column for the command table, cutting inside the enumerated mode list rather than at a word/item boundary.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/help.rs (command-table description truncation)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Reword the summary to lead with the mode list so truncation cannot hide modes, e.g. 'Emulate geo, offline, headers, media, or device (CDP emulation)'.
- Or make the truncation item-aware for backtick-separated lists.

issues.title: delete-data reports only 'User data deleted for session' — no session name, no list of what was deleted

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 -s emu cookie-set b4test cookievalue
./b4w.ps1 -s emu localstorage-set b4key b4value
./b4w.ps1 -s emu delete-data

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: AC8: the command reports what it deleted (which stores, for which session).

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: 'User data deleted for session' (exit 0) — the session is unnamed, and it is not stated whether cookies, localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB and/or cache were cleared. The deletion itself works (verified: after reload document.cookie is empty and localStorage.length is 0, session still usable).

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: A static success message; the underlying handler knows the session id but the message is not parameterized with it or with the cleared store list.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: backend handler for the delete-data tool (MCPToolController / AgentToolManager) and the CLI print path in cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Include the session name/id and the cleared stores in the result, e.g. 'Deleted cookies (3), localStorage (1 entry) for session emu'.
- Mention explicitly that emulation overrides are NOT cleared by delete-data (they are tab state, not session data) — users may reasonably expect otherwise.

issues.title: set device --mobile does not change the user agent (desktop UA under mobile emulation)

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 -s emu set device --width 390 --height 844 --dpr 2 --mobile
./b4w.ps1 -s emu eval "navigator.userAgent"

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: A 'mobile device' emulation either presents a mobile UA or documents that the UA is left untouched.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: navigator.userAgent stays 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) ... Chrome/155.0.0.0 Safari/537.36' while maxTouchPoints becomes 10. Any site that branches on the UA sees a desktop Windows browser on a 390x844 touch device — the classic inconsistent-fingerprint combination.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The device branch issues only Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride (width/height/deviceScaleFactor/mobile); Emulation.setUserAgentOverride is never sent, and the --mobile option only drives the mobile flag of the metrics override.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/commands.rs:2386-2394 (CommandDef set, tool_params_fn, "device" branch) and the option definition for --mobile at commands.rs:2345

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Either set a matching mobile UA when --mobile is given (add --ua for an explicit override, and a way to restore the original UA),
- or state in help that --mobile enables touch metrics only and the user agent is unchanged, so nobody assumes a full device profile.

issues.title: network requests dumps tens of KB of raw JSON for the whole session with no default limit or human-readable view

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 -s emu network requests
# -> 48.2 KB single-line JSON array (requests from every page visited in the tab), truncated by the terminal harness; --filter/--type/--status exist but the default view is unfiltered and unbounded

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: A compact default listing (id, method, status, type, URL) with the full envelope behind --json, plus a limit/paging option.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: A raw JSON blob including full request/response headers and timing for every tracked request; on the first call it even contained the previous page's document request. There is no --limit and no summary line, so the signal (which request do I care about?) is buried.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: network requests prints the backend's raw JSON array without CLI-side formatting, and the tracked buffer spans the tab's history rather than the last navigation.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/commands.rs (network requests CommandDef) and the backend networkRequests handler

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Print a table by default (short request id, method, status, resource type, URL) and reserve raw JSON for --json.
- Add --limit <n> (newest first) and indicate the total count and buffer window in the header.
- Consider scoping the default view to the current document unless --all is passed.
